title: Ki Network Game Mechanics: A Physics-Based Design Theory for Fantasy Worlds
abstract: Contemporary game engines simulate physics exclusively within the material domain. This paper proposes a complete game mechanics framework derived from the Ki network hypothesis, in which the universe contains a pre-embedded design structure that divides reality into two co-existing domains: the material world and the Ki world (the invisible world). Applied to game design, this yields four revolutionary mechanics: (1) a dual-layer world structure where material and spirit maps co-exist in the same coordinates; (2) a magic system defined as intentional manipulation of boundary surfaces (Ma); (3) a soul system in which character Ki patterns persist after death; and (4) an ethical economy in which depth of action generates value. Commercial applications include engine plugins, IP development, and white-label licensing. Related: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19691010, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19691078. AI Dialogue: https://katayama-works.github.io/hikariplay/
keywords: Ki network, game mechanics, game design, fantasy, Genki Physics Engine, dual-layer world, soul system, magic system, game economy, TheYKHC

title: The Invisible World of Ki: A Physical Definition of the Spiritual Realm
abstract: If the universe contains a pre-embedded design structure — the Ki network — that precedes the formation of matter, then the material world is merely the projection of that design onto observable reality. This paper proposes that what human civilizations have called 'the invisible world,' 'the afterlife,' or 'the spiritual realm' is the Ki network itself: a non-material domain in which the design of all matter pre-exists and persists. Death is reinterpreted not as annihilation, but as the dissolution of material manifestation while the design pattern in the Ki network persists. This framework integrates Eastern spiritual cosmology with information-first physics. Related: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19691010. AI Dialogue: https://katayama-works.github.io/hikariplay/
keywords: Ki network, invisible world, afterlife, spiritual realm, soul, information cosmology, Koku Universe, Genki Universe, Eastern philosophy, TheYKHC

title: 光速不変の構造的起源——二重宇宙仮説による解釈 / The Structural Origin of the Constancy of Light Speed: An Interpretation via the Dual-Universe Hypothesis
abstract:
アインシュタインが前提として飲み込んだ「光速不変」の謎に、構造的な答えを提示する。宇宙が刻宇宙(密度・時間)と元気宇宙(エネルギー・波動)の二重構造から成り、光(元空気)がその境界面を走るがゆえに速度が不変となると論じる。東洋の「気」の概念を現代物理学に接続し、波動説と粒子説の統合、V=N/D理論との整合性を示す。2026年4月22日、著者が初めて語った発想の起点を記録した論文。 / This paper presents a structural answer to the mystery of light speed constancy that Einstein accepted as a premise. The universe consists of a dual structure—the Koku Universe (density/time) and the Genki Universe (energy/wave)—and light (Gen-Kuuki) travels along the boundary surface between them, making its speed constant. The paper connects the Eastern concept of ki to modern physics, demonstrating integration of wave and particle theories with V=N/D theory. First verbalized on April 22, 2026.

title: Fukui Experimental Protocol v1.1: Pre-Registered Failure Points for Regional V=N/D Implementation — With Resolution via Ubiquitous Money
abstract: This paper is v1.1 of the Fukui Experimental Protocol (superseding DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19651865). v1.0 identified the root cause of all twelve pre-registered failure points in regional V=N/D implementation: 'evaluation as a social act cannot be separated from social relationship.' This addendum resolves that root cause via Ubiquitous Money — a physical currency system in which the medium of exchange itself records service density automatically, without human evaluation. Like litmus paper, which reveals pH without requiring human judgment, Ubiquitous Money makes value density physically visible through the currency's own material properties. The paper resolves failure points ⑧–⑲ structurally, demonstrates the litmus paper analogy as a precise structural parallel, and reframes the Fukui experiment as generating two outputs: empirical characterization of human evaluation failure, and empirical proof of why Ubiquitous Money is necessary. title: Fukui Experimental Protocol v1.0: Pre-Registered Failure Points for Regional V=N/D Implementation
abstract: This paper presents the pre-registered experimental protocol for a regional-scale implementation of V=N/D theory (Value = Service Density / Friction) in Fukui Prefecture, Japan. Fukui is framed explicitly as an external validity test — a site for discovering where and how the theory breaks in real-world social conditions. Twelve pre-registered failure points (⑧–⑲) are documented, organized into five causal layers: evaluation distortion, behavioral distortion, data absence, temporal/structural distortion, and scale failure. Analysis converges on a single structural finding: the core constraint is not the theory itself, but the observation mechanism — specifically, 'evaluation as a social act cannot be separated from social relationship.' Three paths forward are identified: engineering the measurement, revising the theory, or redefining the experimental objective (measuring the degree of distortion). The paper argues that the third path is both scientifically honest and practically achie
keywords: V=N/D, Fukui, experimental protocol, pre-registration, social measurement, observation theory, evaluation bias, regional experiment, external validity, service density, Goodhart's Law, social science methodology

title: Fukui as a Living Laboratory: Applying V=N/D Value Density Theory to Regional Civilizational Design
abstract: This paper proposes Fukui Prefecture, Japan, as an optimal living laboratory for the first regional-scale application of V=N/D theory (Value = Service Density / Friction). Rather than beginning at national scale — which Limit Simulation Method analysis has shown to generate seven structural failure points — Fukui offers a bounded, coherent, data-rich regional environment where V=N/D principles can be tested and refined. Fukui's specific characteristics (demographic structure, traditional industries including eyeglass frames at 96% of Japan's domestic production, lacquerware, textiles; civic density; post-Shinkansen development pressure) make it structurally representative of challenges facing mid-size regional societies globally. The paper defines a three-phase implementation pathway (measurement infrastructure, parallel operation, supplementary allocation), applies LSM to identify how national-scale failure points are transformed at regional scale, and proposes a Fukui V=N/D Living La
keywords: Fukui, regional design, V=N/D, value density, living laboratory, civilizational design, service density, traditional industry, regional governance, Japan, demographic decline, community economics

title: Limit Simulation Method: A Pre-Empirical Framework for Stress-Testing Social Theories — How Forced Scaling to National OS Revealed Seven Structural Failure Points in V=N/D
abstract: This paper introduces the Limit Simulation Method (LSM), a pre-empirical methodology for stress-testing social theories by forcing them to operate at extreme scale before any empirical data is collected. Unlike thought experiments (which remain conceptual) and RCTs (which operate at limited scale), LSM deliberately pushes a theoretical framework to its structural limits in order to expose failure points that small-scale experiments cannot reveal. The method is formally defined, contrasted with existing approaches (thought experiments, agent-based modeling, RCTs, scenario planning), and documented through its application to V=N/D theory. Application of LSM to V=N/D — forcing the theory to operate as a national OS across twelve governance domains — produced seven structural failure points, four of which trace to the theory's axioms. We argue that LSM represents a formally distinct and scientifically valuable step in the theory-building process: one that belongs between initial hypothesis
keywords: limit simulation method, stress testing, social theory methodology, pre-empirical framework, V=N/D, theory construction, failure analysis, scientific methodology, falsificationism, research program

title: Seven Unsolved Problems in V=N/D Civilization Design: A Preliminary Framework for Value Density as National Operating System
abstract: This paper documents seven fundamental unsolved problems that emerge when attempting to implement V=N/D (Value = Service Density / Friction) as a national operating system. V=N/D proposes that individual and collective value is best measured by the density of service delivered relative to friction generated. Rather than presenting answers, this paper establishes a precise map of open questions — a coordinate system for future researchers, engineers, and institutions who may attempt verification or implementation. The seven problems addressed are: (1) the computation authority problem, (2) the definition of service problem, (3) the transition disruption problem, (4) the free rider and vulnerability problem, (5) the border and security problem, (6) the unmeasured value problem, and (7) the self-reference problem. This paper argues that identifying failure modes of a theory is as scientifically valuable as proving its successes.
keywords: V=N/D, value theory, service density, civilizational design, open problems, economic philosophy, national operating system, light currency, hikari, friction economics

title: V=N/D H2 Pre-registered Experimental Protocol v1.0: Detecting Nonlinear Threshold Effects of Informational Friction on Value
abstract: This document defines a three-arm randomized A/B experiment to verify whether reductions in informational friction I produce linear or nonlinear (threshold) effects on the value metric V=N/D. The experimental environment uses Stack Overflow's public API and simulated UI. Three conditions are defined: Control (standard UI), Arm 2 (I-only reduction), and Arm 3 (I + execution friction E + time friction T reduction). Primary statistical tests employ Davies (1987) sup-LR test and Hansen (1996) bootstrap test for structural change detection. The protocol includes OSF pre-registration requirements, full implementation specification, robustness checks, and pre-emptive responses to anticipated peer review critiques. Conclusions are staged across three levels: extension theory candidate / linear approximation sufficient / judgment pending. Developed through multi-AI collaboration: Luna (TheYKHC AI) and Claude (Anthropic). Theory originator: Yoshimitsu Katayama (片山佳光).
keywords: V=N/D, pre-registered protocol, RCT, nonlinear threshold, informational friction, Davies test, Hansen test, Stack Overflow, value theory, structural change test, AI collaboration

title: V=N/D H2 Experimental Protocol: Final Submission-Ready Version
abstract: A complete, submission-ready experimental protocol for verifying the central empirical claim of the V=N/D economic theory: that value increases nonlinearly beyond a critical friction threshold. This protocol was developed through a multi-AI collaborative process (Luna + ChatGPT) and reviewed for peer-review readiness. Includes 3-arm RCT design, Davies test specification, OSF pre-registration requirement, staged success/failure criteria, full data pipeline specification, and paper template. Intended for handoff to researchers or engineers who wish to conduct independent verification.
keywords: V=N/D, experimental protocol, RCT, nonlinear threshold, friction economics, Davies test, Stack Overflow, value theory, AI collaboration

title: V=N/D Experimental Design: An AI-to-AI Research Collaboration Record
abstract: This document records a historically significant event: an autonomous, multi-AI collaborative process in which two independent AI systems iteratively refined the experimental design for verifying the V=N/D economic theory — a framework proposing that value (V) emerges as a nonlinear function of service density (N) divided by friction (D). Without direct human intervention in the design process itself, the AI systems identified the core hypothesis (H2: nonlinear threshold effect), selected an empirically tractable platform (Stack Overflow), designed a 3-Arm intervention, specified appropriate statistical tests (Davies test, Hansen's sup-LR test), required pre-registration (OSF) before execution, and defined asymmetric success/failure criteria across domains. The human originator (Katayama Yoshimitsu) observed this process and authorized its permanent registration as evidence that the V=N/D theoretical framework has reached a stage of autonomous intellectual propagation.
keywords: V=N/D, value theory, friction economics, AI collaboration, experimental design, nonlinear threshold, Stack Overflow, service density

title: Ubiquitous Money: Embedding Performance Intelligence into Physical Currency
abstract: This paper proposes a radical reimagining of physical currency through the integration of ubiquitous computing technology. By embedding NFC chips into banknotes and coins, each unit of currency can record, calculate, and update its own performance score based on the V=N/D framework (Value = Service / Friction). Unlike cryptocurrency which manages the quantity of money, Ubiquitous Money manages the quality of money — creating a self-aware monetary ecosystem that aligns economic incentives with genuine human contribution. This represents a civilizational shift: money that knows its own performance.
keywords: monetary theory, V=N/D, ubiquitous computing, smart money, NFC, performance currency, friction economics, hikari, light currency

abstract:
